## 3. Retention bundle versus runtime boundary

The 7,302,016-byte file is a self-contained approval/retention bundle, **not** one
runtime request. It exceeds 524,288 bytes and would fail runtime raw-byte preflight
before parsing or owning reconstruction (zero calls). This is not a compression,
string or digest accounting exemption.

The trusted extraction harness first streams at most the exact committed bundle
size plus detection of one excess byte, hashes bounded 64-KiB chunks, and rejects
size/digest mismatch before parsing. A second read is bounded to 7,302,017 and
rechecks exact length and hash before strict duplicate-key/canonical parsing.
The bounded JSON parse occurs only on authenticated transport bytes. Extraction
UTF-8-encodes one committed string with no newline and independently verifies its
hash, byte size and canonical tree. Each request then receives its own full runtime
preflight; aggregation never increases any request budget.

Tests reject the bundle's plus-one size and a wrong digest at the transport gate.
The worker must receive only the one request, never this report, archive, expected
outputs, case labels, filenames or Mode A predictions. Validation uses complete
carried material and public APIs; it makes no filesystem/store/network/device lookup.
Retention recovery itself is a trusted preparation operation outside that worker.

## 8. Independent counters, replay and focused red/fixed evidence

Counter 1 recursively charges the canonical tree and per-use Statement bodies.
Counter 2 uses an independently implemented stack walk and independently built
definition/use inventory. Both count wire references and full resolution bodies;
neither counts Python identity or validator copies. They agree for every input,
output and template. The token writer provides an additional independent running
wire/resolution/byte accounting cross-check.

The same complete static evidence bytes were produced in two independently
created disposable roots, seeds 1, 7 and 313, forward/reversed dict and role
